clue.text: What may prevent one seeing waterfalls?

definitions.meaning: clouding of the eye's lens that blocks sight

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an eye condition clouding the lens and a great cascade of water, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Chronic crashes on eastern coast road

indicators.note: something that crashes is smashed to pieces, so the letters of the word before it are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A habitual car crash on a road running along the eastern shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chronic' reads as describing the crashes, but it is the word whose letters are rearranged by 'crashes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coastline, like those on the Riviera.

clue.text: Beginning to tie silver label

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of tie is taken

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Starting to attach a silver luggage label.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a small label tied or stuck onto something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Send race official over

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters of the race official's title are read backwards

parts.note: a timer is the official who times a race

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a race official across somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send or transmit, as with money or a case passed to another court.

clue.text: Conservative on team helping to gain respect

parts.note: Con is the usual abbreviation for a Conservative politician
a side is a team in sport
a ration is a portion or helping of food

explanation.surface: A Conservative serving on a team in order to earn some respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Consideration is thoughtful regard for others, a synonym of respect.

clue.text: Fresh in, a star singer

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of in a star are made into something new

explanation.surface: A newcomer arrives, a star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges the letters of IN A STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the famous American crooner, an example of a singer.

clue.text: Naughty child, one occupying seat next to one

indicators.note: placed beside, so one piece sits alongside the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament holds a seat in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A naughty child sits in a chair beside someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seat' is a parliamentary one, so its occupant is an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous little devil, used of a badly behaved youngster.

clue.text: Individuals entering former crown colony that's become a republic

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the individuals are placed within the colony's name

parts.note: India was formerly under the British Crown
ones are individual units or people

explanation.surface: People settling in an old British possession that has since become a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a sovereign state governed as a republic, an example of one.

clue.text: Character's parking technique

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
an art is a skill or technique

explanation.surface: Someone's way of parking a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A part is a role or character played by an actor.

clue.text: Most of army unit's recommended diet

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter

parts.note: a regiment is a unit of the army

explanation.surface: Much of a military unit follows the advised eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter T from REGIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet or exercise for health.

clue.text: Lowest point in Florida now receding

indicators.note: receding says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Florida is now at its worst moment, like a falling tide.
explanation.walkthrough: The concealed run RIDAN spans 'Florida now'; 'receding' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the bottom-most point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: At one's office, bought bar of gold

parts.note: a party in office is said to be in
got means obtained or bought

explanation.surface: Someone at work buys a gold bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast block of metal, typically gold or silver.

clue.text: One used in experiment in African country by greedy person

parts.note: Guinea is a country in West Africa
a pig is a glutton

explanation.surface: A test subject in Africa, beside a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: A guinea pig is a rodent long used in labs, hence anyone used as a test subject.

clue.text: Under canvas, firmly fixed?

definitions.meaning: camping, inside a tent, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The word means determined, and split in two it describes being inside a canvas shelter.

clue.text: Arrangement made by George, getting me shot

parts.note: Geo is a short form of the name George
taken as written
a try is an attempt, or shot

explanation.surface: George sets something up and the photographer gets a picture of me.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry can mean the configuration or shape of parts, as in a car's suspension geometry.

clue.text: Emperor acknowledges English girl embracing empress firstly

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: hails means greets or acknowledges

indicators.note: firstly asks for the first letter of the word empress

parts.note: lassie is a Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: An emperor greets an English girl who is hugging the empress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' wraps the whole string HAILS-E-LASSIE round the initial of 'empress', which lands after HAIL. Haile Selassie was the last Emperor of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Haile Selassie ruled Ethiopia as its last emperor, an example of one.

clue.text: Witty remark, gem, pair in convulsions

indicators.note: in convulsions means thrashing about, so the letters of gem and pair are jumbled

explanation.surface: A joke so good that a couple are doubled up laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, clever saying, a pithy witticism.

clue.text: Holy city's name appearing in newspapers, etc.

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the other word

parts.note: the media are newspapers, television and the like

explanation.surface: A holy city is named in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia is Islam's second holiest city, an example of a holy city.

clue.text: Warning a member about lake

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the lake

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Cautioning someone about the state of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is an alert or warning signal of danger.

clue.text: In which you'll find this range of mountains?

definitions.text: In which you'll find this range of mountains?

parts.words: In which you'll find this range of mountains?
parts.note: a book of maps shows mountain ranges

explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps would show a mountain range, and the North African range bears the same name.

clue.text: Port not opened or finished

indicators.note: not opened means without its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A wine left unopened, or already drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the wine, but it is the harbour town of Dover; 'not opened' drops its D.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means ended or completed, as in 'the game is over'.

clue.text: Privet cut down, surprisingly revealing snake

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the remaining letters fall into an unexpected order
cut down means shortened, so the last letter of the hedge plant is lopped off

explanation.surface: Trimming a privet hedge, a gardener is startled to find a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims PRIVET to PRIVE, and 'surprisingly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The viper, or adder, is a venomous snake.

clue.text: I caught it sitting by sick criminal

indicators.note: sitting by means placed alongside, so one piece goes next to the other

parts.note: ill means sick
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught an illness from sitting next to a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means unlawful, an adjective synonym of criminal.

clue.text: Prompt for actor — line heard

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word for a line is said rather than spelt

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: An actor's prompt is a line overheard from offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' looks theatrical, but it is a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the signal, often another actor's line, telling a performer to speak or enter.

clue.text: Playwright's doctor

indicators.note: 's means has, so the word holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A dramatist's physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's (has) says the word contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig or doctor something is to falsify or tamper with it; both are verbs.

clue.text: One mostly in control in religious community

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the next piece

parts.note: mastery is command or control

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One person largely runs things in a religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of 'One' before 'in' places what is left inside the word for control.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is the house where a community of monks lives.
